record.context_brief: Classification of singly-even self-dual [48,24,10] codes of type W48,2
record.original_question: Classify all extremal singly-even self-dual [48, 24, 10] codes whose weight enumerator is W48,2 = 1 + 768y^10 + 8592y^12 + 57600y^14 + ··· and whose shadow enumerator begins S48,2 = 54y^8 + 16976y^12 + ···.

evidence.quote: There are two possible weight enumerators W48,1 and W48,2 for extremal singly-even self-dual [48, 24, 10] codes. Namely, ... W48,2 = 1 + 768y10 + 8592y12 + 57600y14 + ··· , S48,2 = 54y8 + 16976y12 + ···
Open Question 9.3. Classify all extremal singly-even self-dual [48, 24, 10] codes with weight enumerator W48,2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A binary linear code $C$ of length $n$ is self-dual if $C = C^\perp$ with respect to the standard inner product on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. It is singly-even (Type I) if all codeword weights are even but not all are divisible by 4. The shadow of a singly-even self-dual code $C$ is $S = C_0^\perp \setminus C$, where $C_0$ is the subcode of codewords of weight divisible by 4. A self-dual code of length $n$ and minimum distance $d$ is called extremal if $d$ attains the maximal value allowed by the Mallows–Sloane bound; for Type I codes of length $48$ this maximum is $10$.

It is known that there are exactly two possible weight enumerators for extremal singly-even self-dual $[48,24,10]$ codes. Consider the second one, namely
$$W(y) \;=\; 1 + 768\,y^{10} + 8592\,y^{12} + 57600\,y^{14} + \cdots,$$
together with the corresponding shadow weight enumerator
$$S(y) \;=\; 54\,y^{8} + 16976\,y^{12} + \cdots .$$

Classify, up to equivalence, all extremal singly-even self-dual binary $[48,24,10]$ codes whose Hamming weight enumerator equals $W(y)$ (equivalently, whose shadow enumerator equals $S(y)$).
artifact.status_search_result: Searches for a classification of extremal singly-even self-dual [48,24,10] codes with weight enumerator W48,2 reveal only partial results: examples and constructions of such codes (e.g., codes attaining the second weight enumerator) and classifications under additional automorphism-group assumptions (odd prime order automorphisms), but no complete classification appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Classification of Binary Self-Dual [48,24,10] Codes with an Automorphism of Odd Prime Order
status_evidence.snippet: Classification restricted to codes admitting an automorphism of odd prime order, not a full classification.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial classifications under automorphism assumptions exist.

status_evidence.title: Binary extremal self-dual codes of length 60 and related codes
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs singly-even self-dual [48,24,10] codes with previously unknown weight enumerators, but does not classify them.
status_evidence.claim: Constructions of W48,2 codes exist but no classification is given.
